interview.hardest_part: Getting through the first night: the model must notice the light failing, gather grass and twigs early, and build a campfire or torch in time. The crafting UI requires pointer hover and a left click on the correct entry, which is easy to fumble from screenshots. Afterwards, sustaining food (berries, carrots, seeds) while managing a daily fire, and resisting the urge to explore too far from resources, is the second-hardest loop.
interview.likely_failure: Death to darkness on night one (Charlie's attack) while still learning the crafting panel, or starving around day two or three after exhausting nearby berry bushes. Also plausible: losing health to a spider nest or hounds, or wandering off-screen while a screenshot-latency delay eats into the brief dusk warning. Since points reset on death and one episode must reach all milestones, any single early death zeroes the day-based score.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Abundant early food sources (berry bushes, carrots, seeds) that need no cooking; grass and twigs everywhere for a torch and campfire; the context action (Space) picking up and harvesting nearby items automatically; the Long Day option extending daylight, giving more time to gather; hunger draining slowly enough that casual foraging can sustain the first two days; recipes for torch, campfire, and axe being simple and early in the crafting tree.
interview.harmful_mechanics: The night cycle is instantly lethal without a light source, and dusk shortens gathering time; crafting and inventory are mouse-hover and click heavy, which is error-prone from static screenshots with delayed responses; held inputs for 3 seconds make precise movement and kiting difficult; hunger, sanity, and health are all slowly decaying pressures; hostile mobs (hounds, spiders) can interrupt gathering; and the scoring is all-or-nothing per episode, so a single death before the fifth day wipes out accumulated day milestones.
